issues.body: The tool_update doc says a request failing on operation K leaves operations `1..K` applied. The engine's non-atomic contract does not guarantee that K completed: earlier operations are retained, while K itself may be partly applied or not applied. The new PodStore documentation in this same diff states that distinction correctly, so the MCP-facing documentation is inconsistent and can mislead callers about post-error state.
issues.fix_hint: Replace `leaves operations 1..K applied` with wording matching PodStore: operations before K remain applied; K itself is not guaranteed either to be fully applied or to have applied nothing; later operations do not run. The module-level wording `partially-applied prefix` can remain.
issues.title: MCP update documentation still overstates what remains applied at operation K

verdict.summary: The round-2 security defect is fixed: update_inner now reconciles WAC/ACP after a partially applied error, and the new multi-operation regression test exercises the real retained-prefix path and verifies that a subsequent write is denied after an ACL revocation. One public MCP doc comment still states the partial-apply contract incorrectly by saying operations 1..K remain applied, even though operation K may be partly applied or not applied; the more precise PodStore documentation already says this correctly. Progress is improving because the prior major implementation/test gap is resolved and only this documentation inconsistency remains.
